summary: End-to-end review of the Employees bulk-upload (.xlsx) feature. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests PASS (sample-template, .xlsx-only enforcement, missing-header rejection, full-success insert + GET regression, partial processing across 9 error categories, manager-not-found rejection, upload-history list+detail+xlsx error-report, auth 401/403, single-create regression with and without optional dept/desig/location). Manually verified 403 with non-Super-Admin (manager@ticketing.com) on /sample-template and /upload-history. Frontend: full happy-path verified live — toolbar buttons render, modal opens with title 'Upload Employees (.xlsx)', template download triggers (6551 bytes), .xlsx upload → upload-result with Total/Success/Failed cards + Download Error Report button, Upload History modal lists past sessions with status pills + Report links, CSV file is rejected with toast 'Only .xlsx files are supported' and the Upload button stays disabled.

minor.issue: In-file duplicate Email / Employee-Code rows are reported as 'Email already exists in system' / 'Employee Code already exists in system' instead of 'Duplicate Email/Employee Code in upload file'. Root cause: the first occurrence is inserted, then its email/emp_id is added to existing_emails/existing_emp_ids BEFORE the second row is checked, so the in-file branch is unreachable when the first row is itself valid. The dup is still detected (counted as Failed) but the user-facing reason is misleading.

No teams are seeded in the test DB, so the happy-path manager-email-to-team attach branch (member_ids $addToSet) could not be exercised end-to-end. Only the negative case (Manager Email not among existing Team Managers) was verified.

issues: The error-toast for CSV rejection is rendered as a generic 'Action failed' header with the real reason below in smaller text. The user has to read the second line to know what went wrong. Consider promoting 'Only .xlsx files are supported' to the toast title.

Upload-result preview lists only first ~5 rows of errors inline ('Error preview (2 of N)') which is fine, but the table has no column separation for Row/Email/Reason — Reason wraps and the columns visually merge. Minor.

action_items: Optional (LOW): improve in-file-duplicate error reason — check `email in seen_emails` BEFORE `email in existing_emails` so the user sees 'Duplicate Email in upload file' for row N when row N-1 in the same file used the same email. Same for emp_id.
Seed at least one team with a known manager so the happy-path manager-email → team.member_ids attachment can be regression-tested end-to-end (currently only the negative path is covered).
(Nice-to-have) Surface the rejection reason in the toast TITLE instead of the body for CSV / non-xlsx selection.
critical_code_review_comments: contact_uploads.py — in-file duplicate detection branch is logically unreachable for the common case because existing_emails is mutated immediately after each successful insert; reorder the if/elif so seen_emails is checked first.

contact_uploads.py L287 — `if manager_email and not row_errors` means a row with both a bad date AND a bad manager email will only report the date error. Manager-email lookup is silently skipped when any other validation fails. Consider always validating manager email so the error report tells the user every reason in one pass.

contact_uploads.py L221 — async-for over the entire contacts collection to build existing_emails/existing_emp_ids on every upload. Fine for small tenants, but at 10k+ employees this becomes the dominant cost. Add an index hint or paginate.

contact_uploads.py L411 — `errors[:5000]` cap and `truncated_errors` flag are good defensive limits, but the API response (line 431) inlines `errors[:50]`, while the upload session document persists up to 5000. The frontend has no way to know the difference; consider returning `total_errors` separately from the inlined slice length.

contact_uploads.py — sequential email-send loop after all inserts blocks the HTTP response. For a 1000-row upload with SMTP latency of 200ms this means a 200s response. Push to the existing notifications outbox queue and return immediately (current code already calls send_email which writes to outbox, but the loop is still sequential and runs inside the request).

core.py L547 — Legacy role aliases ('Manager', 'Research', etc.) are migrated to 'Admin' on startup, but VALID_ROLES in contact_uploads.py only accepts {'Super Admin', 'Admin'}. The error message says 'Role must be one of: Admin, Super Admin' which is correct, but the SAMPLE template's Instructions sheet should call out that ONLY these two roles are accepted — currently it just says 'One of: Super Admin, Admin' which is fine, just double-check copy.

contact_uploads.py L97 — Endpoint declarations are physically ordered inside router file, but `server.py` must import contact_uploads BEFORE contacts.py because contacts.py declares GET /contacts/{contact_id} which would shadow /contacts/sample-template etc. A comment/guard is in place but a regression-test for this ordering would prevent future breakage. (Verified ordering is currently correct — sample-template returns 200, not 404.)

success_rate.backend: 100% (13/13 pytest tests pass; +2 manual curl 403 checks pass)
success_rate.frontend: 100% on the 6 P0 scenarios listed in the request

test_credentials: admin@ticketing.com / Admin@123 (Super Admin) — verified. manager@ticketing.com / Test@123 — verified used as non-Super-Admin for 403 checks. Note: after the v3 role collapse the manager account's stored role is 'Admin', not 'Manager'.
seed_data_creation: Tests insert ~5 TEST_-prefixed contacts via the public POST /api/contacts and POST /api/contacts/bulk-upload endpoints; not cleaned up (the bulk-upload endpoint does not expose a delete-by-prefix). The created rows are visible in the Employee List as 'Alice Bulk', 'Bob Bulk', 'Dup Email A', 'Dup Emp A', 'Exist Person' etc. Safe to remove via the existing Delete Employee action if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests are at /app/backend/tests/test_contact_bulk_upload.py — run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2) pytest backend/tests/test_contact_bulk_upload.py -v`. Frontend testids that exist on /admin/contacts: open-bulk-upload-btn, upload-history-btn, download-sample-template-btn, upload-dropzone, upload-file-input, start-upload-btn, upload-result, upload-total, upload-success, upload-failed, download-error-report-btn, upload-history-table. Login uses 'Sign in' button (not 'Login'). The sample template's two pre-filled emails (aarav.sharma@example.com, priya.iyer@example.com) are already inserted in the DB from prior runs, so re-uploading the unmodified template will produce Status=Failed with both rows reporting 'already exists'. To get a clean Completed-status run, edit the rows or use the test fixture which generates UUID-suffixed emails.
rca_of_the_issue: No critical issue to RCA. The single minor finding is the misleading 'already exists' message for true in-file duplicates — RCA documented in backend_issues.minor[0]: existing_emails / existing_emp_ids is mutated immediately after the first successful insert, so when the in-file-second occurrence is checked the 'existing' branch fires before the 'seen_emails' branch can. Trivial fix: swap the order of the two if/elif checks.
